how: One reader (the builder of the figure, a language model) read, for each of the 60 latents of the browser's random list, its three strongest examples, two sampled firings between a quarter and a half of its peak, two below a quarter, its five most frequent tokens and the five tokens its direction raises most. A latent counts as 'one' if one short description (a word in a context, a role in the sentence, a kind of word, a piece of a word, a place in the text) fits the strongest examples and the samples above a quarter of the peak; stray firings below a quarter of the peak were tolerated. Otherwise 'mixed'. One pass, no second reader, no score of agreement.
